topics.title: Netherlands Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: Dutch ordinary naturalisation combines five years of qualifying residence with integration, suitable residence status and normally renunciation of other citizenships.
topics.scope: Selected ordinary adult naturalisation requirements for residents applying through a Netherlands municipality; option, overseas and shortened family routes are separate.
topics.jurisdiction: Kingdom of the Netherlands: Dutch nationality

facts.label: Five consecutive qualifying years
facts.text: The ordinary baseline is five consecutive years in the Kingdom with lawful residence and timely permit extensions. Exceptions allow earlier applications; five years is an eligibility condition, not a processing-time promise.
facts.locator: Requirements: consecutive residence and exceptions to the five-year term

constraint.cohort: Ordinary adult route; continuous qualifying residence, with separate statutory exceptions

facts.label: Qualifying status throughout the process
facts.text: At application, during processing and at the ceremony, an accepted residence status is required. These include permanent residence, a non-temporary purpose, qualifying EU-family residence, EU-law residence and Withdrawal Agreement status; not every temporary permit qualifies.
facts.locator: Requirements: listed residence categories and validity at ceremony

facts.label: A2 Dutch and civic integration
facts.text: IND requires integration at at least A2, covering reading, listening, writing and speaking alongside civic components. Accepted diplomas and formal exemptions or dispensations can satisfy or modify the exam requirement; these need supporting evidence.
facts.locator: What is the civic integration requirement; exam components; exemptions and dispensations

facts.label: Adult identity and public-order checks
facts.text: Applicants must be at least 18, establish identity and nationality, and not threaten public order or national security. The municipality checks the application and supporting documents before IND assessment.
facts.locator: Requirements; process step 3

facts.label: Renunciation with defined exceptions
facts.text: Adults normally renounce other citizenships after becoming Dutch. Exceptions include a Dutch spouse or registered partner at the decree date and specified protection statuses. Other nationality laws can still cause automatic loss; assess each nationality before applying.
facts.locator: Renouncing nationality is required; exceptions; country list

facts.label: Approval is not the final step
facts.text: After approval and the Royal Decree, attend the naturalisation ceremony and make the declaration of solidarity. IND requires attendance within one year of the positive decision; the approval letter alone does not grant citizenship.
facts.locator: After the positive decision: Royal Decree, obligatory ceremony, declaration

limits: The IND requirements reviewed in September 2026 still state five years and A2. No proposed longer residence period or higher language level is substituted for current requirements.
Option, minor, family and overseas routes and Caribbean examination arrangements need their own assessment. This is not a complete personal application checklist.

topics.title: Netherlands Tax Residence and Foreign Income
topics.summary: Dutch resident and non-resident obligations differ. Worldwide income reporting does not mean every foreign receipt is ultimately taxed twice.
topics.scope: Baseline individual income-tax guidance for moving to, living in or earning income from the European Netherlands; no treaty-residence ruling or rate calculation.

facts.label: Moving to live in the Netherlands
facts.text: The Tax Administration's immigration guidance treats a move to live in the Netherlands as the start of resident-taxpayer status. Before the move, a person may be non-resident or outside Dutch tax scope. A passport is not a substitute for assessing the actual situation.
facts.locator: Your tax liability changes

facts.label: Worldwide reporting and treaty relief
facts.text: Residents report Dutch and foreign income. Whether the foreign portion is taxed in the Netherlands depends on applicable allocation and relief rules; reporting worldwide income is not the same as owing Dutch tax on every component.
facts.locator: Filing a tax return: worldwide income and double tax relief

facts.label: Dutch-source obligations can remain
facts.text: Non-residents report income taxable in the Netherlands, with treaty exemptions assessed separately. Dutch real estate and related rights can remain in scope; non-resident box 3 treatment does not generally include a Dutch bank account merely because it is Dutch.
facts.locator: Filing as a non-resident; state your property in box 3

facts.label: Returns and insurance are separate checks
facts.text: The migration year has a dedicated return procedure. Even without a filing letter, check whether tax is due or refundable. National-insurance and healthcare contributions depend on social-insurance coverage, not simply citizenship.
facts.locator: Your tax liability changes; filing an income tax return; social security

limits: This does not resolve disputed or dual tax residence, an expatriate concession, box 3 litigation or annual rates. Obtain case-specific advice for those questions.
Caribbean tax jurisdictions, corporate tax, inheritance and gift tax are not covered by this European-Netherlands income-tax baseline.

topics.title: New Zealand Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: New Zealand's usual citizenship-by-grant route requires five years as a qualifying resident, specific physical presence, basic English and good character.
topics.scope: Selected usual adult citizenship-by-grant requirements; not citizenship by birth or descent, special Samoan provisions or discretionary waivers.

facts.label: Five years as a qualifying resident
facts.text: Ordinarily, the preceding five years must be under status allowing indefinite residence. Any resident-visa conditions must be met or cancelled. Australian citizens and permanent residents also need five years living in New Zealand under this guidance.
facts.locator: Presence requirement 1: residence visas, multiple permits and Australian residents

constraint.cohort: Ordinary grant route: qualifying indefinite residence, not five years on any visa

facts.label: 1,350 days and a yearly minimum
facts.text: Within the five years counted back from application, presence as a resident must reach 1,350 days overall and at least 240 days in each twelve-month period. Meeting only the overall total is insufficient.
facts.locator: Presence requirement 2: overall and each twelve-month period

constraint.cohort: Ordinary grant route; also at least 240 days in each twelve-month period

facts.label: Intention to remain connected
facts.text: Applicants normally intend to keep living in New Zealand. Specified overseas employment or accompanying a New Zealand spouse or partner on Crown service can qualify instead; ordinary plans to settle abroad are not automatically equivalent.
facts.locator: Presence requirement 3; planning to live outside New Zealand

facts.label: Basic conversational English
facts.text: Applicants need basic conversational English. Non-native speakers provide accepted evidence such as school, employment or language-test records; a case officer may interview them. No fixed IELTS score or CEFR level is asserted by this guidance.
facts.locator: Opening requirement; if English is not your first language

facts.label: Character and disclosure
facts.text: Good character is assessed separately. Pending charges, recent convictions, imprisonment, protection orders and other specified conduct can affect approval. Required disclosures and any requested overseas police clearances must not be omitted.
facts.locator: Crimes and investigations; declarations; overseas residence

facts.label: Citizenship test planned for late 2027
facts.text: Currently applicants declare that they understand citizenship responsibilities and privileges. A test is planned for most grant applications from late 2027, not current applications. The reviewed announcement does not yet fix the exact start date or final procedural details.
facts.locator: Opening announcement; about the citizenship test

limits: Residence, physical presence and processing time are different measures. Individual waivers, children and special Samoan routes require separate assessment.
Recheck the announced 2027 test before applying; no exact effective date is invented and it is not presented as a current requirement.

topics.title: New Zealand Tax Residence and Foreign Income
topics.summary: New Zealand generally taxes residents on worldwide income, with separate rules for transitional residents, qualifying visitors and non-resident source income.
topics.scope: Selected individual residence and income-scope rules, including Inland Revenue's June 2026 visitor and transitional-residence guidance; not a personal tax determination.

facts.label: Home ties or more than 183 days
facts.text: Residence generally begins at a permanent place of abode or more than 183 days in any twelve months, whichever occurs first. Partial days count as present; the day test backdates residence. Qualifying non-resident visitors and specified workers have exceptions.
facts.locator: Becoming resident; day counting; permanent place of abode; seasonal workers

facts.label: A tightly qualified visitor exception
facts.text: The visitor rule allows up to 275 days in any eighteen-month period only if all conditions hold: not a New Zealand tax or transitional resident before qualifying; not working for or paid by a New Zealand resident or a non-resident employer's New Zealand branch; no local sales or location-dependent work; neither partner receives Working for Families; lawful presence; and tax liability in another country of residence.
facts.locator: Non-resident visitors: all listed conditions

facts.label: Leaving does not immediately end residence
facts.text: Ordinary non-residence requires both no permanent place of abode and more than 325 days absent in twelve months, with specific counting and backdating rules. Overseas New Zealand-government service has a separate continuing-residence rule.
facts.locator: Knowing when you become non-resident; counting days; government service

facts.label: Residents generally report worldwide income
facts.text: Foreign income is generally taxable even if retained abroad or already taxed overseas. Foreign-tax credits and treaties may provide relief; overseas-employer salary is not automatically exempt.
facts.locator: How worldwide income is taxed; double tax agreements; employment

facts.label: One-off transitional exemption
facts.text: Eligible new or returning residents with no New Zealand tax residence in the preceding ten years can receive a one-off exemption for most foreign income for roughly four years. Foreign employment and personal-services income are excluded. Opting out or specified Working for Families applications can end it early; exact dates require separate calculation.
facts.locator: Qualifying; early ending; exempt and non-exempt income; start and end dates

facts.label: New Zealand source income still matters
facts.text: Non-residents generally remain taxable on New Zealand-source income. Withholding can apply to interest, dividends and royalties; treaties and the kind of income affect liability and whether a return is required.
facts.locator: Opening rule; double tax agreements; withholding; filing

limits: Tax residence is different from nationality and immigration permission. The visitor exception is not blanket tax-free remote-work permission.

Property-sale rules, investment-fund calculations, tax rates, trusts and superannuation are outside this baseline. Confirm current rules and personal treaty treatment with Inland Revenue or a qualified adviser.
